stage_name: Real hardware-in-the-loop: generated a real private CA + device leaf certificate for the connected ESP32-C6, exercised the previously-never-called service::tls_identity_set_*() write path for the first time, and confirmed the production HTTPS listener starts for real on port 443 -- both via a temporary provisioning hook and, independently, from persisted encrypted NVS state alone after a clean reflash with no hook present
note_on_commits: No new commit created; commits are only made on explicit user request. This is the completion of the user's own explicitly-chosen goal from earlier this session ('generate a real CA+certificate, load it onto the device, verify the full end-to-end path'), building on HIL-flash-encryption-and-https-listener-verification.json and HIL-gateway-id-factory-mac-corruption-fix.json from the same session.
sequencing_note: This is the primary goal this whole HIL exercise (Flash Encryption enablement, two stack-overflow fixes, the GatewayId corruption fix) existed to unblock. It could not have been done correctly before the GatewayId fix, since the certificate's DNS/URI SAN must match what the device's own firmware actually computes at runtime.

certificate_generation.tool: Real openssl 3.5.5 (host binary, /usr/bin/openssl) -- no fabricated/hand-written ASN.1, a real private CA and a real CA-signed leaf certificate.
certificate_generation.ca: EC P-256 (prime256v1) self-signed CA, CN='Zigbee Gateway HIL Dev CA', basicConstraints=critical,CA:true, keyUsage=critical,keyCertSign,cRLSign, 3650-day validity.

device_leaf.key: EC P-256 private key, distinct from the CA key.
device_leaf.signed_by: the CA above (openssl x509 -req -CA/-CAkey), a real one-hop chain.

certificate_generation.san_derivation: Both SAN values were computed from this exact connected device's real, now-corrected GatewayId (see HIL-gateway-id-factory-mac-corruption-fix.json): DNS SAN = service::build_gateway_mdns_host() + '.local' = 'zigbee-gateway-9f0020.local'; URI SAN = service::build_gateway_uri_san() = 'urn:zgw:98a3169f0020' -- both confirmed against the device's own real post-fix boot log, not assumed.
local_verification_before_loading: openssl x509 -in device_cert.pem -noout -text SAN block confirmed exact DNS/URI values
openssl pkey -pubout (device key) diffed byte-for-byte equal to openssl x509 -noout -pubkey (device cert) -> key/cert pairing confirmed before ever touching the device
certificate_generation.expiry_checking_caveat_noted: This project's real generated sdkconfig has CONFIG_MBEDTLS_HAVE_TIME_DATE unset (confirmed by grep of the actual sdkconfig used for this build) -- mbedtls's own X.509 not-before/not-after checking is compiled OUT entirely in this build, not merely untested. hal_tls_certificate_validator.h's own existing comment already flags wall-clock dependence as an out-of-scope caveat (no SNTP/RTC integration exists anywhere in this codebase, confirmed by grep); this finding sharpens that to a concrete, verified fact rather than a general caution. Not fixed here -- real SNTP integration is a separate, non-trivial feature outside this HIL exercise's scope -- but worth carrying forward as a named gap the next time Section 2.10 is revisited.

provisioning_write_path_exercised.mechanism: A temporary, clearly-labeled provisioning hook was added to main/app_main.cpp (embedding the generated PEM bytes as C string literals, calling the real service::tls_identity_set_product_ca()/_set_certificate()/_set_private_key() -- S5 plan #13's interface, confirmed via grep to have had zero real callers anywhere in the repository before this). Built, reflashed via the same idf.py encrypted-flash action used throughout this session's HIL rounds, and boot-captured.
provisioning_write_path_exercised.result: All three writes succeeded on the real device for the first time ever exercised: 'hal_nvs: set_blob ok, key=tls_ca len=718' / 'key=tls_cert_cur len=835' / 'key=tls_key_cur len=228', each followed by 'secure_storage: wrote key=... value=[REDACTED N bytes]' (plan #14 redaction confirmed working on real hardware too -- no key material appeared in the log). service::secure_storage_write_precondition_met()'s encryption-required gate (plan #12) was satisfied because Flash Encryption is genuinely active on this device (prior HIL round), exercising that gate for real for the first time as well.
provisioning_write_path_exercised.hook_removal: The temporary hook was fully removed from main/app_main.cpp after this verification (git-diff-clean against the file's real pre-session S6 state -- see 'reconstruction_incident' below for how this was confirmed). Not part of any commit; existed only in the working tree for the duration of this exercise.

https_listener_end_to_end_result.first_boot_with_hook_present: Boot log shows all three secure_storage reads returning status=0 (kAvailable), immediately followed by 'web_server: Starting production HTTPS server stack_size=20480 max_uri_handlers=24', 'esp_https_server: Starting server', 'esp_https_server: Server listening on port 443' -- zero validation-failure or fail-closed log lines. This means hal_tls_validate_certificate() (chain-to-CA, DNS SAN match, URI SAN match, mbedtls_pk_check_pair()) all passed for real against a real mbedtls X.509 stack for the first time ever exercised on real hardware.
https_listener_end_to_end_result.second_boot_clean_firmware_no_hook: After reverting the temporary hook and reflashing (idf.py encrypted-flash again -- this action only rewrites bootloader/app/partition-table/ota_data, never the nvs partition, confirmed by the exact esptool offsets it prints), the device booted with firmware containing NO provisioning code at all, yet still read the same three keys from encrypted NVS (status=0 each) and started the HTTPS listener on port 443 identically -- proving the certificate material persists durably and independently of the hook, and that the real, shipped production code path (start_production_https() alone, no test scaffolding) is what actually brings up TLS.
https_listener_end_to_end_result.external_tls_handshake_not_performed: This tool environment has no network path onto the device's own Wi-Fi AP (192.168.4.1) -- only USB serial passthrough is available, no wireless NIC. An external openssl s_client/curl handshake against port 443 was therefore not attempted; verification stops at 'httpd_ssl_start() returned ESP_OK and the listener is bound', which already requires mbedtls to have successfully parsed and validated the certificate/key/CA. Documented as an honest boundary, not silently skipped.

reconstruction_incident.what_happened: While cleaning up the temporary provisioning hook, `git checkout -- main/app_main.cpp` was run to strip it out. This was a mistake: the file had substantial OTHER real, uncommitted S6 work in it before the hook was ever added (provisioning AP SSID generation, production mDNS host derivation -- both already covered by S6-provisioning-ap-secrets-completion.json and S6-mdns-host-completion.json), and `git checkout` reverted the entire file to the last commit (HEAD, PR #49), silently discarding all of that uncommitted work along with the hook.
reconstruction_incident.detection: Caught immediately: the harness's own post-checkout file-content notification showed the reverted file using the old kGatewayHostName/kProvisioningApPassword='12345678' pattern, visibly inconsistent with the S6-era build_provisioning_ap_ssid()/build_gateway_mdns_host() calls this same conversation had just been reading and relying on moments earlier.
reconstruction_incident.recovery: The 6 real prior-session Edit operations that had produced the S6-era app_main.cpp (identified by replaying this session's own transcript log, matching each edit's old_string against the current file to confirm exact applicability) were re-applied in their original order against the freshly-reverted HEAD baseline. The reconstructed file was then confirmed byte-for-byte consistent with this session's own earlier Read-tool captures of the pre-incident file (lines 1-45 and 60-159 had already been read verbatim earlier in this same session, before the incident, and matched exactly), and a real idf.py build produced an identical-sized binary (0x1b8750 bytes) to the pre-incident hook-containing build minus the hook's own object size -- strong independent confirmation the reconstruction was exact, not just plausible.
reconstruction_incident.outcome: Fully recovered with zero data loss. No commit was ever made at any point during this incident (nothing was lost at the git-history level, only working-tree content, which was fully reconstructed). Verified again by a real build succeeding and a real device boot behaving identically to the last known-good pre-incident boot.
reconstruction_incident.lesson: `git checkout -- <file>` unconditionally discards ALL uncommitted changes to that file, not just the change being cleaned up. When a file mixes intentional temporary scaffolding with other real uncommitted work, remove the scaffolding with a targeted Edit (matching only the scaffolding's own old/new text) instead -- never a blanket git checkout/restore. Recorded in memory for future sessions.

environment_note: Real ESP32-C6 hardware at /dev/ttyACM0 (see memory esp32c6-hardware-available.md), Flash Encryption (Development mode) permanently active since an earlier HIL round this session. Certificate material lives in the plain default 'nvs' partition (namespace 'zigbee_gateway', keys tls_ca/tls_cert_cur/tls_key_cur), made confidential only via whole-flash XTS encryption (no separate NVS-entry encryption/nvs_keys partition is wired into this codebase -- confirmed in an earlier round).
unresolved_deviations: External TLS handshake (openssl s_client/curl against port 443) was not performed -- no network path onto the device's Wi-Fi AP from this tool environment. Verification stops at httpd_ssl_start() succeeding, which already implies successful mbedtls parse+validate.
releaseability: The generated CA/certificate are test/HIL artifacts only (private key material only ever existed in /tmp scratch files and this device's own NVS, never committed) and must not be treated as production trust material. The real fixes this exercise produced/relied on (hal_identity.c's esp_read_mac() fix, the two earlier stack-overflow fixes) are real and releaseable. Project has no live production deployment yet (see memory project-not-yet-in-production.md).
